basis: Two consequential row descriptions require correction. The remaining 29 row classifications are confirmed against the captured HEAD with independent TS and TSX ast-grep scans plus literal/raw-SQL and DDL corroboration.

supersessions.correction: The value is genuinely write-only, but the active owner design explicitly assigns it diagnostic provenance: `connection_ref` is the immutable original id for diagnosis and must never bypass a null FK. This is not unassigned dead storage. The schema lacks an adjacent reasoned `@column-ok` marker, so the current lens finding should be resolved by adding the diagnostic exemption or explicitly reversing that design decision.
supersessions.independent_search: ast-grep found no `embedGenerations.connectionRef` member read in 4,061 production TS files or 807 production TSX files; rg found only the schema, baseline, writer, fixtures, and the active design's diagnostic ruling.

supersessions.correction: The classification is correct but the producer account is not. Production does not call `.values(speakerRows)`. It writes `digest_id` with Drizzle INSERT ... SELECT, selecting `chatDigests.id` and the aliased character id once per speaker. This row belongs to the same insert-select blind-spot class as the embed-space-state and refinery rows.
supersessions.independent_search: rg found the sole production insert at queries.ts:394 followed by `.select(...)`; ast-grep independently found the direct digestId consumers in embeddings, chat memory, search display/scope, and handoff-restamp.

scanner_blind_spots: embed_space_state.owner_id and scope are written by INSERT ... SELECT at space-state.ts:91-112 and directly consumed by active-space, nearest, conflict, promotion, PK/FK/CHECK logic.
plugin_kv.plugin_id, owner_id, and key are written by raw atomic INSERTs at plugin-kv.ts:60-66 and 125-129 and directly consumed on every scoped operation.

refinery_schemas.id, owner_id, and created_at are written by INSERT ... SELECT at queries.ts:346-371; id and owner scope mutations/reads, while createdAt reaches schemaSummaryOf through the typed row carrier.
imagery_wiring_at_captured_head: HEAD:imagery persistence InsertGenerationInput and values omit provider and connectionId.
HEAD:generate-core receives `req.connection`, but passes only model/cost/time/image into persistImage and therefore never writes either attribution field.
The schema and domain-freshness-plane explicitly retain the fields as attribution, so the null population is a wiring defect rather than rot.
dormant_or_parked: chat_stream_events has no production insert: ast-grep scanned 2,130 production TS and 695 TSX files with zero writer matches; the planted test scope found the two fixture writers. The schema header explicitly records retention and the replay/bounds consumers are live.
session_entries.connection_id is explicitly nullable until the per-user agent-sdk cut-over writer lands; its FK, child index, and partial unique index already consume the column.
ddl_consumers: provider_rows origin columns participate in the origin-shape CHECK, FK actions, and FK scan indexes.
admin_distributed_plugins.distributed_by participates in CASCADE lifecycle and its child index; its value is intentionally omitted from the projected admin view.
session_entries.is_primary is the predicate of session_entries_primary_unique.
write_only_or_dead: No production TS or TSX member reads were found for chatHandoffResumptions.updatedAt, themeClusters.centroid, embedGenerationTargets.updatedAt, embedSpaceState.completedAt, or pluginAssets.fetchedAt; targeted rg/raw-SQL searches corroborated the absence.
theme_clusters.centroid has only a producer plus schema/fixture round-trip assertions; no persisted-centroid consumer exists.
plugin_assets.fetched_at and the two embedding timestamps have explicit or timestamp-shaped provenance but no value consumer; they need a reasoned exemption or removal decision as reported.
default_provenance: session_entries.created_at is DB-defaulted timestamp provenance; direct table-member searches found no production read, while broad row-shape hits are homonyms.
migration_behavior: The migration directory contains only 0000_baseline.sql, meta/0000_snapshot.json, and meta/_journal.json with one journal entry and 103 snapshot tables.
The current repository doctrine says post-launch schema cleanup uses a forward incremental migration and does not patch the frozen baseline.

concurrent_worktree_evidence.observation: The shared worktree contains concurrent uncommitted imagery-attribution edits. They add providerId/connectionId to InsertGenerationInput, pass req.connection.providerId/connectionId through generate-core, and write imageryGenerations.provider/connectionId.
concurrent_worktree_evidence.effect: Those edits appear to repair both captured-HEAD imagery wiring defects, but they are not part of HEAD 3a2e348d and were not counted as refuting the report. No test verdict for the concurrent repair is claimed here.

material_limitations: No pnpm ast, whole-repo typecheck, or heap-heavy TypeScript program was run, per the brief. The report's own completed 103-table/31-hit corpus receipt was treated as the candidate denominator, then consequential claims were independently checked with ast-grep and rg.

The shared worktree was mutable. All captured-report judgments used HEAD snapshots where concurrent imagery edits overlapped the report; other rows were checked against files with no relevant working-tree diff.

No runtime database suite was run because the review is about static producer/consumer classification and the shared tree contains concurrent changes. DDL semantics were verified from schema source plus baseline/snapshot text.

chat_handoff_resumptions.created_at is outside the 31-row candidate set but is the identical insert-once timestamp sibling of updated_at and has no value consumer. Any removal decision for updated_at should adjudicate the pair; the original report notes this but does not classify the sibling.

positive_controls: chatHandoffResumptions.chatId returned production and test consumers while updatedAt returned none.
The chatStreamEvents insert pattern returned the two test fixture writers while returning zero production writers.
Direct member patterns returned the expected live reads for every scanner-blind-spot column.
